speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me understand what might be causing this, how long do these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient is a 70-year-old woman with sudden, position-dependent vertigo and presbycusis. Do you experience any auditory symptoms like ringing in the ears or a feeling of fullness in your ear during these episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The position-dependent nature of your vertigo, combined with your age and lack of other auditory symptoms like tinnitus or ear fullness, strongly suggests BPPV. This is typically caused by displaced otoconia in the inner ear. Do you have any history of recent head trauma or surgery?
